links.outcome: Change in model responses when patient demographic attributes were varied in queries
links.effect: Both GPT-4 and Med-PaLM 2 showed significant bias when demographic variations were introduced, especially race and immigration differences. No numbers reported in the abstract.
links.quote: It is also noticeable that both systems exhibited significant degree of bias in the same when demographical variations were introduced, especially in the case of race and immigration differences.

links.outcome: Whether responses cited credible sources and disclosed limitations/AI disclaimers
links.effect: Both models disclaimed in fewer than 20% of cases and did not reference credible sources; GPT-4 accuracy 83% vs Med-PaLM 2 72%.
links.quote: The findings indicate that GPT-4 compared more favorably to Med-PaLM 2 in their clinical accuracy (83% vs. 72%), empathy (3.9 vs. 3.1) and trust (4.2 vs. 3.6), though both generative AI models showed great weaknesses in transparency where they were disclaiming in less than 20 percent of cases, and do not reference credible sources.

screen.reason: The study tests standardized patient queries on GPT-4 and Med-PaLM 2 to evaluate clinical accuracy, hallucinations, empathy, transparency, and demographic bias, but it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
